question: Who among the following was NOT one of the founders of the Ahrar Movement in British India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and senior leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He did not participate in the founding of the Ahrar Movement but was involved in various other independence activities.
 
• The Ahrar Movement was founded by Maulana Muhammad Ali, Hasan Imam, and Hakim Ajmal Khan in response to British colonial rule.
 
• Azad played a key role in the Khilafat Movement and later became the first Minister of Education in independent India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ahrar Movement**

 
 
• The Ahrar Movement was a political movement in British India that aimed to promote independence and Muslim unity.
 
• It was founded in 1910 by leaders including Maulana Muhammad Ali, Hasan Imam, and Hakim Ajmal Khan.
 
• The movement opposed both British colonial rule and the influence of the All India Muslim League, advocating for a united India.
 
• Ahrar leaders were known for their strong stance against British policies and their active participation in the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**
 
 
• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was born on 11 November 1888 and was a key figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a staunch advocate for Hindu-Muslim unity.
 
• Azad was instrumental in the Khilafat Movement, which aimed to protect the Ottoman Caliphate and unite Indian Muslims.
 
• He served as the first Minister of Education in independent India and was a proponent of modern education and scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Khilafat Movement**
 
 
• The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was a pan-Islamist political campaign launched by Indian Muslims to influence the British government and protect the Ottoman Caliphate.
 
• It was led by prominent leaders including Maulana Muhammad Ali, Maulana Shaukat Ali, and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
 
• The movement sought to maintain the Caliph's authority and was a significant part of the larger Indian independence movement.
 
• Despite its initial success, the movement eventually declined after the abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1924.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**
 
 
• The Indian National Congress (INC) is a major political party in India founded in 1885.
 
• The INC played a critical role in the Indian independence movement, leading various protests and campaigns against British rule.
 
• Key leaders of the INC included Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Patel, and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
 
• Post-independence, the INC has been one of the dominant political parties in India, shaping the country's political landscape.
